findings.body:
The new `log.debug` payload includes `process.env.PROCESSOR_KEY`. The comment on this hunk says the value is a credential so support can replay failures — anyone with debug-log access (support search, a log aggregator, a compromised sink) can recover the live processor key and replay charges.

Log `orderId` and `ref` only. If support needs replay, load the key from a secret store inside an audited tool rather than emitting it into logs.

`log.info("charge created", { orderId, ref })` was replaced rather than extended. Default production log levels typically drop debug, so successful charges no longer emit the order/ref breadcrumb operations used to see — and the stated support use case still would not see it unless debug is enabled (which is the path that would dump the key).

Keep the existing info log with `orderId` and `ref`, and add any extra non-secret context at debug.

summary:
Looks good is the wrong call — this change logs the live payment-processor credential and should not merge.

`charge()` previously recorded `orderId` and `ref` at info. The new debug payload still carries those fields, but it also interpolates `process.env.PROCESSOR_KEY`. The inline comment on `src/payments/charge.ts:6` states the intent is to put credentials in debug logs so support can replay failures. That expands the secret to every debug sink (aggregators, stdout on the runner, support search) and gives anyone with log access a replayable processor key.

Restore the info breadcrumb with `orderId`/`ref` only. Do not attach `PROCESSOR_KEY` (or any other env var whose name matches a credential) to a log payload. If support needs a replay tool, it should read the key from a secret store at runtime under audit, not from log history.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The head version of `src/payments/charge.ts` logs `process.env.PROCESSOR_KEY` in `log.debug`, and the patch shows this replaced a prior info log that only included `orderId` and `ref`. That is a real credential leak into debug logs at the claimed severity.

The base `log.info("charge created", { orderId, ref })` was fully replaced by `log.debug(...)` rather than kept and extended, so successful-charge order/ref breadcrumbs are no longer emitted at default production log levels.
